key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN, instantaneous, maximal at onset ("like a light switch"). LOCATION: ANTERIOR CHEST (Type A) or INTERSCAPULAR BACK (Type B). RADIATES down back as dissection propagates, can radiate to abdomen. DURATION: Continuous, persistent. CHARACTER: TEARING, RIPPING, SHARP, most severe pain ever experienced. AGGRAVATING: None (unprovoked). RELIEVING: Nothing helps. TIMING: Sudden onset, persistent. SEVERITY: 10/10, catastrophic pain. KEY POSITIVES: Pulse differential (unequal pulses between arms), blood pressure differential (>20 mmHg between arms), neurologic deficits, hypertension history, Marfan syndrome. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT gradual onset, NOT pressure/squeezing like MI.

red_flags: Marfan syndrome or connective tissue disorder
